statement: The point $(1, 5)$ lies on the graph of $y = f(x)$. The function $g$ is defined by $g(x) = f(x - 4) + 2$. Which of the following points must lie on the graph of $y = g(x)$?

choices.misconception: I moved the point the wrong way in both directions, 4 to the left and 2 down.
I moved the point 4 to the left because I saw minus 4, but subtracting 4 inside the function shifts the graph to the right.
I shifted the point 4 to the right correctly, but I moved it down 2 instead of up 2.

hints: Ask which input to $g$ makes the expression inside $f$ equal to $1$.

solutions.reliable: We need the input of $f$ to be $1$: $x - 4 = 1$ gives $x = 5$. Then $g(5) = f(1) + 2 = 5 + 2 = 7$, so the point $(5, 7)$ is on the graph of $g$.
solutions.elegant: $f(x - 4)$ shifts the graph $4$ units right, and adding $2$ shifts it $2$ units up, so $(1, 5)$ moves to $(5, 7)$.
